note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 by an independent auditor who authored none of 816ce1ce4c, 2cbd255ba4, 2e5c2d012a, d22b811ce4 or 1a2ccaeef8 (phase 5 of spec-filter-wire-0-umbrella, the per-peer text filter chain deleted). RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4 read: "If a BGP speaker is configured to alter the value of the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute received over EBGP, then altering the value MUST be done prior to determining the degree of preference of the route and prior to performing route selection (Decision Process phases 1 and 2)." The moved unit TestRFC4271ReceivedMEDAlteredBeforeTheDecisionProcess replaced the text delta "med 10" answer with the typed set answerSet("med","10") from a filter that declares med read and set: The test filter is now an answerTransport behind filterTransportSeam, compiled by answerPolicy into a policychain library chain, so the verdict travels the real filter-update path (route.Input, rpc.FilterUpdateOutput decoded by the library chain) instead of the deleted policyFilterSeam that handed a PolicyResponse straight to the text chain; that is the production path every plugin filter now takes. It still feeds an EBGP UPDATE with MED 100 through notifyMessageReceiver with the import chain step and requires exactly one dispatch carrying MED 10 in both RawBytes and WireUpdate.Payload, so an alteration applied after dispatch, or not at all, goes red. Single-polarity scope unchanged. Ran the tagged units under ./le job run at HEAD (-tags ze_bgp, -v): PASS (scratch audit-p5-units-v.log). Verdict unchanged: enforced.
